prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scope
- Applies mainly to England due to devolution. Scottish and Welsh proposals may differ.

Fiscal approach and tax
- Reprioritise about £5bn annually by abolishing certain subsidies and departments/functions, cancelling ID cards, and diverting Child Trust Fund money to education.
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate only on earnings above £100,000 to fund: abolition of university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled people; and cutting local taxes by replacing Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay.
- Independent scrutiny of budgets by the National Audit Office; greater ONS independence.
- Typical household local tax bill reduced by about £450 under Local Income Tax.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via expanded access to scans/tests, weekend/evening operation, and staffing/training.
- Free eye and dental checks; broaden prescription charge exemptions for long‑term conditions.
- More clinicians; scrap central targets; more local accountability.
- NHS dentistry contract reform and personal dental plans.
- Health MOTs, personal care plans for long‑term conditions, stronger mental health rights, end age discrimination.
- Public health: school nutrition standards, limit junk‑food ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top‑up fees; restore grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund budget to hire 21,000 teachers; infant classes average 20, junior 25; extended school hours; 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Subject-specialist teaching in core subjects; reduce high‑stakes testing at 7 and 11; stronger SEN support; behaviour plans and managed transfers.
- Unified academic/vocational diplomas from 14; fund parity for colleges; maintain statutory school transport distances.
- Green building standards for education estates; strengthen outdoor learning.

Crime, justice, borders and equality
- 10,000 more police (funded by scrapping ID cards) plus complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy, modernise tech.
- Prioritise serious drug crime; expand tough community sentences; anti‑social behaviour tools with underlying support.
- Prisons focused on work, literacy and skills; progress tied to effort.
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; tighten judicial control of any control orders; allow intercept evidence; repeal flawed terror provisions.
- Overhaul asylum processing via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; pursue EU common standards.
- Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units in every force.

Economy and business
- Stamp Duty threshold to £150,000.
- Simpler, lighter regulation with impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspections.
- Small‑business rate relief and site‑value rating; fair‑trading duty; English Tourism Board.
- Carbon Tax replacing the Climate Change Levy; incentives for cleaner vehicles and energy‑efficient homes.
- At least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no replacement of aging nuclear plants.

Pensions, benefits and family support
- From 75: basic state pension to at least £109.45 (single) and £167.05 (couple), linked to earnings; residency‑based “citizen’s pension.”
- Replace Council Tax to benefit most pensioners; six months’ maternity pay at minimum‑wage rate.
- Tailored employment support replacing one‑size‑fits‑all schemes; end harsh sanctions on genuine claimants.
- Replace the Child Support Agency with HMRC‑based assessment/enforcement plus specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working‑age people; option to invest a year’s payment in insulation.
- Strengthen protection for failed occupational pensions; consult and honour accrued public‑sector pension rights.
- Reduce fraud/error through simplification and prevention.

Housing, local services and environment
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; encourage brownfield reuse via VAT reform; require permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; increase core arts funding with inflation; support grassroots sport.
- Devolve more powers; streamline inspectorates; protect post offices and universal postal service.
- Zero‑waste goal; 60% household recycling within seven years; producer responsibility; climate‑aware planning/building rules.

Transport
- Rail reform with fewer, longer franchises; shift road funds to station safety and key upgrades.
- Reform Vehicle Excise Duty to zero for least‑polluting cars; expand congestion charging tied to upfront public transport investment; long‑term national road pricing to replace fuel duty and VED.
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for pensioners, disabled people, families and youth.
- Limit major new roads; grow rail freight; develop ports/waterways; aviation: per‑aircraft charging, emissions trading, oppose new SE expansions.

Rural, agriculture and fisheries
- Fair‑trading duty and Food Trade Inspector to protect farm gate prices.
- Accelerate CAP reform toward public goods; support family farms and new entrants.
- Marine Act with conservation zones and regional co‑management; stronger wildlife protection.
- Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act.
- Precaution on GM crops, support GM‑free zones, rigorous labelling; promote organic.

Europe, international affairs and defence
- Support EU institutional reform subject to referendum; prepare for euro entry if conditions met.
- Iraq: back democratic transition, build Iraqi capacity, and aim to withdraw forces with UN mandate expiry.
- Multilateral security, UN and EU reform, human rights focus.
- Defence: address overstretch; improve procurement; reprioritise programmes; maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms‑export oversight; back an international arms trade treaty.
- International development: increase aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural dumping; fair trade access; responsible investment; green development priorities; stronger action on global environmental crime; lead on climate targets (Kyoto plus “contraction and convergence”).

Constitution and governance
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; reduce departments/ministers; decentralise to local/regional bodies; fair funding across the UK.
- Extend STV to local and national elections; predominantly elected second chamber; voting age aligned with other civic responsibilities; reform BBC governance via an independent regulator.
- Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; merge key portfolios into a single environment/transport/energy department.
